perf: Food's share of the P1 G7 regression was +0.08 ms/substep (food.safety +0.070 = a GC pass landing there, food.thermal +0.008, food.refresh +0.003; ADOPT 0.149/0.134/0.018 vs P1 0.219/0.142/0.021). Cause of food's own cost: every full thermal pass (each 300 s) and every safety run copied each food record into the journal through World.mut to write a temperature or a spoilage counter. Fix: field-level World.set_quiet for non-structural writes (temperatures, core temperature, food's thermal bookkeeping, the clock counters), as the kernel thermal system does. Measured A/B on two copies of the same live tree differing only in house_sim/systems/food/systems.py, the bench loop of tools/bench_systems.py (40 substeps x seeds 0-3, every system called), five interleaved runs each, best of five, GC disabled so a collection cannot land in one system: food.safety 0.173 -> 0.109 ms, food.thermal 0.155 -> 0.089 ms, food.refresh 0.023 -> 0.023 ms; food total 0.351 -> 0.221 ms/substep (-0.130 ms, -37 %, more than food's +0.08 share). With GC on, best of five: food total 0.765 -> 0.228 ms (A drew a GC pass in food.thermal). GC pass counts in the bench loop are deterministic and alike (gen0 163 vs 157, gen1 15 vs 15, one gen2 pass outside any system in both). tools/bench_systems.py 40 0 1 2 3 --domain food (B, three runs): food.safety 0.109-0.110, food.thermal 0.091-0.092 (one run 0.562 with a GC pass), food.refresh 0.024-0.030 ms. Results unchanged: golden dump --all (243 specs + 8 runs) identical A vs B and HEAD-food vs final; bench-loop, +1 h and 6 h (probes on and off) state digests identical. The machine ran at 100 % CPU from other agents' processes (bench totals 3.6-18 ms/substep run to run), so the absolute G7 total is not re-measured here; idle probes were not the lever (bench_systems calls every system directly).

read on an unfamiliar (novel) thing returns its true type's read-tier fields: realistic scene with thing_1 = all_purpose_flour {novel: true, open: false, size_m [0.2,0.15,0.25], color gray, material plastic} vs chef_knife with the same look: read -> {allergens, date_type, diet_tags, full_g} vs 'There is nothing legible to read on it' (kitchen_scale: {capacity_g, display}). Show an unfamiliar thing's printed text (label_text/text) only, or one refusal, like the NOVEL_FIELDS glance. Probe: scratchpad p1_food/f3/novel_food_probe.py.

Realism._label_substitution rewrites an unfamiliar target's own label and type words anywhere in a domain message, so a generic refusal that happens to name a kind of thing reads differently when the unfamiliar thing is of that kind: weigh target=<unfamiliar kitchen_scale> answered 'Put it on a unfamiliar medium object first' vs 'Put it on a kitchen scale first' for every other unfamiliar thing (food now words that refusal without the noun). Rewrite only references the domain makes to the entity (its label in the message as the domain rendered it), or flag it in the auditor.

registry.lookalike_size_spreads (SPREAD_RESOLUTION_M 1 cm and 5 %) is not the geometric camera's resolution: obs.robot.facing_deg (two decimals) after approach follows the target's true centre, so members 5 mm apart in one dimension still differ in geometric mode (HEAD's measuring_cup group with measuring_cup_half patched to 0.135 m and measuring_cup_third to the quarter's 0.13 m: the third and the quarter become indistinguishable, the half stays apart at approach, look, face and count; 1 cup vs 1/2 cup: facing 41.37 vs 41.55 deg after approach). Either round the facing after approach to the camera's 5-degree bearing grid or lint any size difference.
